cf.title: Bug: Whole-row var in indexes corrupts indexes after DDL

input.subject: Bug: Whole-row var in indexes corrupts indexes after DDL

verdict_reasoning: The goal is not in question: the thread shows index corruption and message #2 lists reports of this class since 2020. The surviving objections are fixable design points about the catalog representation (replication-ondisk-2, maintenance-fit-1) and the missing back-branch plan (replication-ondisk-1). A committer who knows pg_depend and the object address code has to decide on the sentinel subid and the new ObjectType value.

brief.title: Track whole-row Var dependencies in pg_depend to rebuild indexes after DDL
brief.problem: Indexes and constraints whose expressions use a whole-row Var are not rebuilt or revalidated when ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN or ALTER COLUMN TYPE changes the row value of existing rows, so the index becomes corrupt. The author ties this to a4639d64e2 and earlier reports of the same class, and the bug affects any user with such expression indexes or constraints.
brief.proposed_design: The patch records whole-row references as pg_depend entries with a pseudo-subobject, WholeRowAttrNumber. Shape-changing ALTER TABLE uses these entries to find and rebuild dependent indexes and revalidate constraints without scanning all of them. v4 adds a new object type, OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW, so the object address functions can name and decode it.
user_visible_surface: pg_depend rows with refobjsubid = WholeRowAttrNumber (-32768) for whole-row references.
New object types "table whole row" and "foreign table whole row" in pg_describe_object(), pg_identify_object(), pg_identify_object_as_address() and pg_get_object_address().
New OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW value in the ObjectType enum in parsenodes.h, visible to extensions and event triggers.
ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN and ALTER COLUMN TYPE now rebuild indexes and revalidate constraints that use whole-row expressions.
author_claims: The patch fixes index corruption from whole-row expression indexes after shape-changing DDL.
Explicit tracking avoids O(N) dependency scans, which the author calls prohibitively expensive otherwise.
Checking that relfilenode changes is enough testing, because a rebuild reads the table, not the old index.
The ATPostAlterTypeCleanup failure on combined ADD COLUMN and DROP COLUMN already exists in HEAD and needs a separate fix.
brief.thread_state: Andrey Borodin and Xinlei Zhang reviewed and tested; v5 addresses their points and testing shows no new correctness issues. Open: the patch depends on CF 6121 for the combined ALTER TABLE failure, and whole-row partition keys and column renames are left for later.
unclear: The material does not say whether this fix is meant for back-branches, and pg_depend entries for existing objects would need creating on upgrade.
The proposal does not say how pg_upgrade or pg_dump handle the new dependency entries on existing databases.
The material does not say whether docs for the object address functions or pg_depend change; no documentation hunks are shown.
Whole-row partition keys can still leave rows in the wrong partition; no patch to reject them is shown.
Column renames do not trigger rebuilds, though record output can depend on column names.
search_queries: expression index corruption alter column type

objections.title: New refobjsubid value breaks the assumption that a nonzero subid is a column
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch or an extension walks pg_depend and treats any nonzero refobjsubid as an attnum. When it meets -32768 it fails with an error like "column -32768 of relation ... does not exist", or it silently skips the row. The failure shows up only for tables that have whole-row expressions.
objections.argument: Until now refobjsubid was either 0 or a positive attnum. Review found two consumers that missed the new value: process_function_rte_ref() in message #2 and the object address functions in messages #2 and #5. Between v1 and v5 the patch grew from three backend files to seven, adding aclchk.c, dropcmds.c, seclabel.c and event_trigger.c. Nothing makes a missed consumer fail at build time, and the material does not compare this design with other ways to mark whole-row rows in pg_depend.
objections.author_must_show: Which code in core reads refobjsubid, has each place been checked for WholeRowAttrNumber, and why use a magic subid instead of another marker?

critic.reasoning: Messages #2 and #5 show two consumers that missed the new value during review, and the file list grew from three backend files to seven. The thread does not compare the sentinel subid with another marker.

objections.title: OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW adds a public object type that is not a real object
objections.failure_scenario: An extension or event trigger that switches over ObjectType gets OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW after upgrade and errors or ignores it. A later patch adds an ObjectType-wide feature and must decide again what a whole-row "object" means for GRANT, SECURITY LABEL, DROP or COMMENT. Nothing fails at build time if that decision is skipped.
objections.argument: v4 added OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW only to make the pg_identify_object_as_address() round trip work (message #5, message #7). As a result, v5 touches aclchk.c, seclabel.c, dropcmds.c and event_trigger.c, though a whole row cannot be granted, labelled or dropped on its own. Message #7 also notes that "<relkind> column" addresses already fail the round trip for indexes and views, so the round trip does not force a new enum value. A committer would likely ask for a representation that reuses the attribute path with subobject -32768.
objections.author_must_show: Why can the whole-row pseudo-subobject not be encoded through the existing OBJECT_COLUMN address path, without a new ObjectType value seen by extensions and event triggers?

critic.reasoning: Message #7 says the round trip already fails for some "<relkind> column" cases, so it does not by itself require a new ObjectType. The thread gives no reason for wiring a non-object into aclchk.c, seclabel.c and dropcmds.c.

objections.title: Catalog-based bug fix leaves supported branches and their existing indexes uncovered
objections.failure_scenario: A user on a supported back branch has an index on f(t) and runs ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c int. The index is still not rebuilt, so index scans keep returning wrong rows. The user finds out from inconsistent query results, possibly long after the DDL.
objections.argument: The entry is tagged Bugfix, but the fix depends on new pg_depend rows and a new ObjectType value in parsenodes.h. Back branches would need the new rows for every existing index and constraint, plus an ABI change. The material says nothing about back branches, and message #2 shows the same bug class reported since 2020. A committer would likely ask whether a separate fix for released branches is planned, such as a catalog scan during shape-changing DDL.
objections.author_must_show: What fix, if any, do supported back branches get, and how does it handle indexes created before the fix?

critic.reasoning: The entry is tagged Bugfix and message #2 lists reports since 2020, but the thread never mentions back branches. The fix needs pg_depend rows that existing indexes on released branches lack, so the question stands.

refuted.title: Back branches keep the corruption bug and get no fix
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on a released branch has an index on hash_record(t) and runs alter table t add column c int. The index silently goes stale, and wrong query results show up much later. No minor release can carry this fix, because it adds a new pg_depend convention and a new ObjectType value.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, and message #2 lists reports of this class going back to 2020. A new value in the ObjectType enum in parsenodes.h is an ABI change, and existing indexes in released clusters have no whole-row pg_depend rows to find. The thread does not mention back branches at all. [P1] shows that the project back-patches even awkward fixes when stored data is at risk, so a committer would likely ask what the back-branch plan is.
refuted.author_must_show: What fix, if any, is planned for supported branches, for example rejecting or force-rebuilding on shape-changing DDL, and is it meant to ship with this patch?

precedents.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. P1 concerns column aliases in whole-row Var output and must not be used as support for a back-branch plan here.

refuted.title: refobjsubid = -32768 changes the documented pg_depend contract
refuted.failure_scenario: A schema-diff or migration tool joins pg_depend.refobjsubid to pg_attribute.attnum, or treats any nonzero refobjsubid as a column. After upgrade, whole-row dependencies vanish from its inner join or show up as a dependency on a missing column. The tool then orders or drops objects wrongly, and the user finds out when a migration fails.
refuted.argument: Today refobjsubid is either zero or a column number, and the docs say so. v5 adds a negative sentinel, new "table whole row" object type names in four address functions, and a new event trigger object type. No documentation hunk is shown for catalogs or for the object address functions. Message #7 calls OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW "treated like OBJECT_ATTRIBUTE but slightly differently", which is the kind of special case that external readers of pg_depend will not know about.
refuted.author_must_show: Why does recording the existing relation-level dependency, plus a flag or a distinct deptype, not serve the same lookup, and what documentation changes for pg_depend and the address functions?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2, which makes the same sentinel point with evidence from the thread. The inner-join case loses nothing if whole-row references have no column-level pg_depend rows today, and missing documentation hunks are out of scope.

refuted.title: Bug fix depends on catalog rows that existing indexes do not have
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on a back branch installs a minor release with this fix. Their existing whole-row expression index has no WholeRowAttrNumber row in pg_depend, so a later ADD COLUMN still skips the rebuild. The index stays corrupt and they find out from wrong query results.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, and message #2 lists reports of this class going back to 2020. The fix only works when the pg_depend rows exist, and those rows are written when the index or constraint is created. The proposal does not say which branches it targets. It also does not say what fills in the missing rows for objects created before the fix, in a minor release or after pg_upgrade.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this fix meant for master only, and if not, how do indexes and constraints created before the fix get their whole-row pg_depend rows?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1 for the minor-release case. The pg_upgrade part does not hold, because pg_upgrade recreates the schema through pg_dump and restore, which writes the new pg_depend rows.

refuted.title: Each row-changing DDL path must remember to call the rebuild hook
refuted.failure_scenario: A future patch adds a new ALTER TABLE subcommand that changes the row value of existing rows, for example a column reorder or a new kind of generated column. The author does not call RememberWholeRowDependentForRebuilding(). Whole-row indexes go stale, and no test or assertion catches it.
refuted.argument: The thread already shows this pattern. Renames (message #1) and whole-row partition keys (message #2, message #3) are left out of the patch, and the ADD COLUMN plus DROP COLUMN case needs a fix from another patch. The pg_depend rows make the lookup cheap, but the decision that a command changes the row shape stays in each ALTER TABLE path. A committer would likely ask for one central place that decides when whole-row dependents are rebuilt, or a check that fails loudly when a path is missed.
refuted.author_must_show: What makes a future row-shape-changing ALTER TABLE path fail loudly, in tests or assertions, if it does not trigger rebuilds of whole-row dependents?

critic.reasoning: The patch follows the per-subcommand pattern that ALTER COLUMN TYPE already uses in tablecmds.c to remember dependents, so this applies to existing code equally. The cited renames and partition keys are stated scope limits, and none is a missed call.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Existing indexes and constraints get the new pg_depend rows only when pg_upgrade restores the schema.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds pg_depend rows with refobjsubid = WholeRowAttrNumber (-32768).

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW to the ObjectType enum in parsenodes.h, visible to extensions and event triggers.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: v5 touches aclchk.c and seclabel.c to handle OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix, but the fix needs new pg_depend rows and a new enum value.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every reader of refobjsubid and every ObjectType-wide feature must now handle the whole-row case.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which code in core reads refobjsubid, and has each place been checked for WholeRowAttrNumber?
Why does the patch use a sentinel subid instead of another marker in pg_depend, such as a distinct deptype?
Why can the whole-row pseudo-subobject not go through the existing column address path, without a new ObjectType value?
What fix, if any, do supported back branches get, and how does it cover indexes created before the fix?
Will a patch that rejects whole-row partition keys ship with this one, or can mispartitioned rows remain after it?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows pg_depend, the object address functions and the ALTER TABLE rebuild passes in tablecmds.c would have to own it.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new pg_depend convention and a public ObjectType value that every future reader of refobjsubid must handle, with no end date. The owner also signs for the back-branch answer and the interaction with CF 6121.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered review within about a week in message #3 and posted revisions up to v5 in message #9.

priority.reason: Few users have whole-row expression indexes or constraints, but for them the bug is silent index corruption with reports since 2020. The patch is about 37 KiB across dependency.c, objectaddress.c and tablecmds.c, and adds a lasting catalog convention.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review cannot check how aclchk.c, seclabel.c and dropcmds.c treat OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW, or whether every reader of refobjsubid handles -32768. Messages #4 to #9 were not shown in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for ALTER INDEX .. ALTER [COLUMN] col_num {SET,RESET}
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add `alter index ... alter [column] col_num set/reset (...)` so opclass parameters on an index column can be changed after `create index`, using a column number as `set statistics` does. The patch stores the new values in pg_attribute attoptions, checks them with index_opclass_options(), and does not rebuild the index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Changing an opclass parameter such as siglen without a rebuild leaves the index inconsistent with its options. Nathan Bossart reproduced test failures in hstore after `alter index hidx alter column 1 set (siglen=100)`, which went away after a REINDEX. Alexander Korotkov said the known uses for opclass options all need a rebuild and suggested keeping the options immutable until real cases for mutable ones appear. The author agreed the patch was not enough, and the entry was withdrawn.
matched_queries: expression index corruption alter column type
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: All these cases require index rebuild to change the opclass option.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH I think if we really wanted the feature of primary keys with
included columns, we'd have to add it to the PRIMARY KEY syntax rather
than having an ad-hoc ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT USING INDEX command
to replace the index underneath.

precedents_retrieved.title: revamp row-security tracking
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the per-query tracking of whether row security applies with a global queue of row-security nest levels. get_row_security_policies() marks the levels, and higher-level callers such as fireRIRrules() read them, with cleanup after an ERROR.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed objected to the global variables, the hooks into transaction management, and setting the flag far from where RLS policies are applied. He proposed adding a hasRowSecurity output parameter to fireRIRrules() instead. The author wrote that design as v2 but worried it did not go far enough, and later planned to withdraw for lack of interest. Tom Lane replied that the topic needs more thought and suggested other designs, and the visible messages show no work after that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm also not a fan of using global variables in this way, or the
resulting need to hook into the transaction management system to tidy
up. The end result is that the places where the flag is set are moved
further away from where RLS policies are applied, which IMO makes the
code much harder to follow.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent ALTER TABLE DROP NOT NULL on child tables if parent column has it
precedents_retrieved.summary: Prevent ALTER TABLE ... DROP NOT NULL on a child table when the same column in a parent table is marked NOT NULL, so that the constraint can only be dropped from the parent. The patch added a function in pg_inherits.c to list a relation's parents and a new index on pg_inherits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the approach was wrong because it does not help decide whether to propagate DROP NOT NULL from a parent to its children, and pointed to the earlier plan of storing NOT NULL constraints in pg_constraint with inheritance counts as CHECK constraints do. After Vitaly Burovoy reported that he was writing such a patch, which already forbids dropping inherited NOT NULLs, the author withdrew his proposal in favour of that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't sound like the right approach; in particular, it won't really
help for deciding whether to propagate a DROP NOT NULL on a parent rel to
its children.

precedents_retrieved.title: plpgsql - possibility to get element or array type for referenced variable type
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets PL/pgSQL `%TYPE` refer to variables of composite type, including polymorphic parameters. It also adds syntax to derive the array type or the element type of a referenced variable, first as `%ARRAYTYPE`/`%ELEMENTTYPE` and later as `%TYPE[]` and `ELEMENT OF ...%TYPE`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane proposed rejecting this PL/pgSQL-only implementation. He wanted these type operators added to the core grammar's Typename production, so PL/pgSQL would pick them up automatically. Joe Conway and Jim Nasby agreed. The author then found that a reduced patch with only the composite `%TYPE` fix gave too little benefit, and asked for it to be rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I played with the reduced patch, and the benefit without all other things
is negligible. It should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY WHERE clause generated/system column reference
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches make COPY FROM ... WHERE work with generated columns: they expand virtual generated columns in the WHERE clause and compute stored generated columns before the WHERE clause is checked. They also reject system columns other than tableoid in the WHERE clause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed a smaller fix that rejects generated columns in COPY FROM WHERE with a clear error, and left tableoid for a separate thread. He then argued that support should not be added, because generated columns belong to the target table while the WHERE clause filters input data. Masahiko Sawada had shown that computing stored generated columns before the WHERE clause runs them before BEFORE INSERT triggers, so the WHERE clause changes the row the trigger sees.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This seems fundamentally wrong, because generated columns are a
property of the target table, but the COPY WHERE clause is meant to
filter the input data.

precedents_retrieved.title: Introduce the ability to enable/disable indexes using ALTER INDEX
precedents_retrieved.objectors: David Rowley, Robert Treat, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `alter index ... invisible` / `visible` (first proposed as ENABLE/DISABLE) and a `create index ... invisible` option, using a new pg_index flag so the planner ignores the index while it stays maintained and enforces constraints. A boolean GUC, use_invisible_index, lets a session or workload override the flag and use invisible indexes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on the interface. In quoted replies, David Rowley says he would not commit a GUC that overrides what the catalog says, and Robert Treat argues that a cluster-wide DDL is operationally risky and prefers a GUC listing indexes for the planner to ignore. Michael Paquier objects that such a list-based GUC puts schema knowledge into the GUC machinery and does not scale. A DisableIndex hint was merged into pg_hint_plan meanwhile, and the author withdrew the patch, citing a lack of interest in a core feature.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Looks like there may not be enough interest to port any functionality into core.

precedents_retrieved.title: CHECK constraint deferrable Support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets CHECK constraints be declared DEFERRABLE and INITIALLY DEFERRED, as the SQL standard allows, so SET CONSTRAINTS can delay a CHECK until commit. Rows that fail a deferrable CHECK are rechecked at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CHECK implementation assumes constraints are immutable, and the patch does not change that assumption, so he called the feature a toy. Others then argued it should be dropped or combined with deferrable NOT NULL, which Robert Haas and Vik Fearing disputed. Dean Rasheed also reported open bugs, including a deferred constraint that still failed immediately and a wrong constraint-exclusion result. The visible messages do not show why the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I continue to assert that basing this feature on the current CHECK implementation will produce nothing but a toy feature, that's not only of little practical use but will be an active foot-gun for people who expect it to do more than it can.

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P1] reverted column aliases on whole-row Var output because blessed RECORD tuples were stored on disk; that reason does not apply to pg_depend tracking. Message #2 lists earlier reports of this bug class, including prior work on whole-row dependencies for DROP COLUMN and ALTER TYPE, but the thread does not say why that work stopped.

Upgrade itself looks safe from this angle, because pg_upgrade restores the schema with CREATE INDEX, which records the new pg_depend rows. The new constraint revalidation errors on ADD COLUMN are corrections, but the release notes should mention them.
pg_upgrade restores the schema through DDL, so new clusters get the pg_depend rows. No WAL, heap or wire protocol format changes are shown.

The proposal grants no new privilege and adds no new user-callable action. The new rebuilds run inside ALTER TABLE, which only the table owner or a superuser can run, and they evaluate index expressions the same way ALTER COLUMN TYPE and REINDEX already do. The new pg_depend rows and the "table whole row" object type expose only what pg_depend and the attribute address types already show. A reviewer cannot judge from the prose alone how the aclchk.c and seclabel.c changes handle OBJECT_WHOLE_ROW, so that needs a check against the code.
The goal itself is not in question from this angle. Costs fall only on tables with whole-row expressions, and the thread shows repeated field reports of this bug class.

This is a fix for index and constraint corruption inside ALTER TABLE, and no extension, contrib module or user idiom can make core rebuild those indexes after shape-changing DDL. The only alternative in the material is scanning all indexes and constraints on each such DDL; the author rejects it on cost, and that is a design trade-off for other angles. I cannot name an existing mechanism that does this job, and [P1] covers whole-row Var naming, not dependency tracking.

The proposal fixes index corruption, and message #2 lists independent reports of the same bug class from 2020 and 2023, plus a4639d64e2. Each fix costs a shape-changing ALTER TABLE on a table with whole-row index or constraint expressions, so demand is shown and the 'nobody will use it' test does not apply.
